newsitem.title: USA: Polar Air says U.S. awarded new U.S.-Japan route.
newsitem.headline: Polar Air says U.S. awarded new U.S.-Japan route.

text.p: Polar Air Cargo said it has been tentatively awarded a new U.S.-Japan freighter route by the U.S. government.

The airline said in a statement that its proposal to operate six times a week to Osaka from eight U.S. cities was against proposals from three other carriers: Evergreen International Airlines Inc, American International Airways and Gemini Air Cargo.
Assuming the award is confirmed, three-year-old all Polar will serve Osaka from New York (JFK), Los Angeles, Chicago, San Francisco, Atlanta, Miami, Seattle and Anchorage.
Polar did not indicate when it could start service.
The airline, quoting the text of the U.S. government award, said its proposal "offers the most effective use of the valuable U.S.-Japan all-cargo rights".
Polar operates 13 Boeing 747 freighters and plans to add two B-747-200 freighters later this year.
